intro: Divonne-les-Bains is a spa town in the Pays de Gex in France, on the Swiss border about twenty kilometres north of Geneva, under the slopes of the Jura. In the forest on Mont Mourex above it grows a sweet chestnut that the town's own plaque calls the largest and oldest tree of the Divonne forest, about four centuries old and 6.25 metres round. A reader photographed it and sent it to us.
meta_description: The giant sweet chestnut on Mont Mourex above Divonne-les-Bains, near Geneva: about 400 years old, 6.25 metres round, and how to find it.

trees.name: The Giant Chestnut of Mont Mourex

location.address: Forest clearing on Mont Mourex, above Divonne-les-Bains, Ain

trees.story:
"The biggest and oldest tree on Mont Mourex," wrote the reader who sent us this sweet chestnut from the forest above Divonne-les-Bains, with a GPS fix taken at its foot, and the plaque beside it agrees with them.

The plaque, put up by the Office National des Forêts and the town, calls it the largest and certainly the oldest tree of the Divonne forest. It gives the trunk 6.25 metres round at chest height, the tree 26 metres tall and its age about four centuries. Chestnuts were already marked on the land registers here before 1800, it says, and around 1815 a real chestnut culture grew up on these slopes: nuts and flour, honey, tannin for the tanneries, and wood for stakes, barrels and tool handles. Then interest slowly faded, and this one was left to grow.

The reader's photograph shows what four hundred years does to a chestnut. The trunk twists as it rises, its bark running in deep spiralling furrows, and splits high up into crooked limbs that reach out over a clearing of fallen leaves. Picnic tables stand around it, so the forest expects visitors.

Come in late autumn, as the reader did, when the clearing turns copper under it.
trees.how_to_recognise: In a clearing with picnic tables: a single huge chestnut whose furrowed trunk twists as it rises and splits high up into crooked limbs, a small white plaque on a post at its foot.
trees.access: Free. A picnic clearing in the forest on Mont Mourex, reached on forest paths.
